item.research_question: Can high entropy alloys (HEAs) containing actinide elements exhibit superconductivity?
item.test_conditions: temperatures ranging from 0.4 K to 300 K, magnetic fields up to 9 T, and pressures up to 2.3 GPa
key_findings: The material exhibits bulk superconductivity with a transition temperature Tc ≈ 3.2 K
The upper critical field Hc2 is approximately 6.4 T
The material has a body-centered cubic lattice with a lattice constant a = 3.41(1) Å
The uranium f-electrons are delocalized and do not carry a well-defined magnetic moment
The superconducting state is described by the BCS theory within the weak electron-phonon coupling regime
item.mechanism: The superconductivity is likely due to phonon-mediated pairing, with the disorder in the material providing pinning centers for superconducting vortices
item.limitations: The material's superconducting properties are suppressed compared to the Zr-based analogues, possibly due to the introduction of uranium ions
item.future_work: Further studies are needed to understand the impact of uranium valence and disorder on the superconducting properties, and to explore the potential of HEAs as waste forms for radioactive isotopes
quotes: High entropy alloys (HEA) are an unusual class of materials where mixtures of elements are stochastically arrayed on a simple crystalline lattice
The superconducting state is described by the BCS theory within the weak electron-phonon coupling regime

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can high entropy alloys (HEAs) containing actinide elements exhibit superconductivity?. System: [TaNb]0.31(TiUHf)0.69. Processing: arc furnace technique. Test conditions: temperatures ranging from 0.4 K to 300 K, magnetic fields up to 9 T, and pressures up to 2.3 GPa. Findings: The material exhibits bulk superconductivity with a transition temperature Tc ≈ 3.2 K; The upper critical field Hc2 is approximately 6.4 T; The material has a body-centered cubic lattice with a lattice constant a = 3.41(1) Å; The uranium f-electrons are delocalized and do not carry a well-defined magnetic moment; The superconducting state is described by the BCS theory within the weak electron-phonon coupling regime. Mechanism: The superconductivity is likely due to phonon-mediated pairing, with the disorder in the material providing pinning centers for superconducting vortices. Limitations: The material's superconducting properties are suppressed compared to the Zr-based analogues, possibly due to the introduction of uranium ions. Future work: Further studies are needed to understand the impact of uranium valence and disorder on the superconducting properties, and to explore the potential of HEAs as waste forms for radioactive isotopes. Quote: "High entropy alloys (HEA) are an unusual class of materials where mixtures of elements are stochastically arrayed on a simple crystalline lattice"
